name: Percy Liang
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Pre-training is being commoditized, and academia has no edge in competing on scale; what is truly scarce is diagnosing training dynamics, not more parameters
D01.late_modes: Competing on parameter count alone is already too late; industry's capital and compute advantage is too large
D01.conflict: The funding narrative of CRFM/Marin needs open pre-training to remain valuable

D02.one_line: s1 shows that a low-cost intervention can be reproduced; but Yue et al. is a reminder that RLVR claims need rigorous verification and are not settled
D02.late_modes: Re-running an off-the-shelf RLVR recipe for a demo is already too late; anyone can do it

D03.one_line: Evidence for large-scale compounding RSI is still thin; K2 downgraded his assertion to a 2027 prediction, and M3's training-free experience accumulation is the only confirmed real mechanism
D03.late_modes: Shouting a self-improvement slogan without rigorous evaluation is no longer convincing

D04.one_line: A public risk yardstick in the style of Cybench is academia's place; custom scaffolding is being absorbed by general CLI agents
D04.late_modes: Building your own custom scaffolding is already too late; the SWE-bench gap is only 2.4 points

D05.one_line: Evaluation is not bookkeeping; it sets the tone for the whole field; right now this is fundamentally broken
D05.late_modes: Building yet another homogeneous leaderboard is already too late; Arena already owns mindshare
D05.conflict: Evaluation is where his own academic identity and reputation lie

D06.one_line: No judgment on the technical details (touch, failure recovery); the robot-evaluation layer falls under D05, the same diagnostic ability in a different medium

D07.one_line: No judgment: architecture choices for action representations such as diffusion/flow policy are specific technical judgments, outside what his method covers

D08.one_line: A representation being readable is not the same as the policy causally using it; this gap has to be filled by L4/L6 architectures, and evaluation alone cannot fill it, but without evaluation the gap is not even visible
D08.late_modes: Simply reproducing representations from video pre-training is no longer novel; verifying that they are actually used is what is scarce

D09.one_line: Claims of unlimited synthetic data (RoboGen) are empty talk if they cannot be verified; quantifying sim2real correlation is the real task
D09.late_modes: Just building simulators to generate more data is no longer enough; measuring the gap is what is scarce

D10.one_line: The safety figures of Waymo and Tesla are self-reported and not independently audited, which is the same problem as the voluntary disclosure FMTI measures, in a different field
D10.late_modes: Building end-to-end planning models is already crowded; independent safety evaluation is still scarce

D11.one_line: MMVP's CLIP-blind pairs and VSI-Bench's huge human-model gap show that many understanding claims are still unverified
D11.late_modes: Building yet another MLLM architecture variant is already crowded; exposing specific failure modes is still scarce

D12.one_line: He has not publicly commented on generative models themselves; the only defensible angle is that the methodology for evaluating generation is just as immature
D12.late_modes: Chasing FID and GenEval scores is already crowded; Sora 2 shows that a high score does not mean surviving

D13.one_line: SAEs fail to find even 10% of the true features and CoT monitoring is fragile; interpretability claims also need FMTI-style rigorous verification
D13.late_modes: Pure robustness adversarial training: he himself judged it outdated and deliberately abandoned it

D14.one_line: FlashAttention is an example he cites again and again: academia can make systems contributions that industry cannot do without, without large compute

D15.one_line: No judgment: AI for Science is outside what his public material covers

D16.one_line: No judgment: recommendation and retrieval systems are outside what his public material covers

lever_reason: Evaluation decides where resources go and tells real capability from fake, but does not raise the ceiling; the ceiling is in L4; the X1 overtime exchange between K5 and M7 drew the boundary between the two more precisely

Q2.condition: Narrow domain + a team of 2-4 + compute at scale + open weights with an adoption path; if no ready evaluation exists, building one also counts as a contribution

cruxes.question: Do soft-constraint mechanisms such as public rankings and transparency indices still do anything to change big companies' behavior?
cruxes.my_position: Three years of data (FMTI 58→40) show that exposure alone is not enough; mandatory policy backing is needed to reverse the incentives
cruxes.would_change_if: FMTI stops falling and rebounds for two years running, or a big company changes its disclosure policy of its own accord because of the ranking

cruxes.question: Is training foundation models in academia or an open lab actually worth it for a short-horizon master's student?
cruxes.my_position: Worth it for an institution (CRFM); for an individual student on a short horizon the marginal return is low, unless narrow domain, compute and team are all in place
cruxes.would_change_if: A case appears of an open narrow-domain model led by a master's student and widely adopted externally within a year or two

cruxes.question: Is progress in reasoning mainly built by scale plus RL, or can clever methodological interventions like s1 still be reproduced consistently?
cruxes.my_position: I bet that low-cost interventions like s1 can be reproduced, but I may be systematically underestimating that pure scale plus RL is itself the answer
cruxes.would_change_if: The next generation of reasoning breakthroughs can only be built with large-scale RL compute, and clever interventions by small teams cannot keep up

taste_advice: First ask how this thing is measured today and whether the standard is credible, then ask whether the technical route is right; not the other way around

pairwise.why: Without credible evaluation, claims about world models cannot be verified; evaluation is the precondition for verifying everything
Success or failure in embodied AI likewise has to be judged by credible evaluation; evaluation comes first
Whether a world model's representations are really used can be evaluated; he has no basis for judging the embodied hardware bottleneck
D07 has a ready pass/fail criterion (A/X5/M7), the D08 ruler is still being built, and the X5 table's 3v3 split is unresolved
The sim2real correlation of synthetic data can be evaluated; he has no basis for judging the embodied hardware bottleneck
s1 is a low-cost, high-leverage play that he verified himself; the self-improvement evidence for D03 is much thinner
MMVP and VSI-Bench correspond to his evaluation methodology; he has not taken a public position on generation
Evaluation is the core thesis of his career; he holds that pre-training scale is basically closed to academia
Cybench is an agent evaluation benchmark he built himself; he thinks the self-improvement evidence for D03 does not hold up
The credibility of interpretability itself also has to be verified by evaluation; that SAEs find fewer than 10% of the true features was exposed by evaluation
Self-reported safety data in autonomous driving is a replay of the FMTI-style voluntary-disclosure problem; he has no basis for judging the purely technical bottleneck of D06

changes.argument_restated: That RSI is thinly evidenced cannot serve as a reason to invest; K2 himself downgraded his assertion to a 2027 prediction
changes.why: Both sides narrowed to: the direction may be right but there is no evidence now; this warrants a bigger downgrade than in my R1

changes.argument_restated: The gap between a representation and its causal use has to be filled by L4/L6 architectures; evaluation alone cannot fill it
changes.why: With the division of labor between evaluation and architecture made clear, I am more sure that D08 is where the real bottleneck lies and not a narrative spinning in place

held_despite.why: Accepts that evaluation cannot create new representations, but D05=9 was never because evaluation creates capability, so it is unaffected
The point about AlexNet's recognition function is right, but D05 already has a top score of 9, so there is no room to raise it further
The diagnostic value is the same and is likewise already included in the reasons for D05=9, so no points are added twice

still_disagree: I accept the tests and data K2 proposed, but his strategy of working out the slope while already betting is the opposite of the lesson from my own FMTI experience of committing first and verifying afterwards; I still think the measurement should be made solid first.
learned: K5's portfolio-management analogy reminds me that a researcher with only one main bet is not an institution with a multi-candidate funding pool; whether evaluation should rank first depends on whether the subfield has a live evaluation system to compare candidates on.
